functionalObligations.text: Anyone deposits token0 and/or token1 into the pool's two ERC-4626 CollateralTracker vaults and becomes a Panoptic Liquidity Provider holding a pro-rata claim, whose capital is lent to option sellers.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core#readme (CollateralTracker, ERC-4626, five actor roles) at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api readme); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/contracts/smart-contracts-overview (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: `Pl` carries the corpus's marker: the pool lends *positions* into Uniswap rather than fungible assets to a borrower who wants leverage. Also relevant to L2's exit-liquidity clause, discharged here by `Sl` (F17).

functionalObligations.text: Each CollateralTracker maintains its own market state including a global borrow index, so a lender's claim accrues compound interest without a transfer.
functionalObligations.evidence: contracts/types/MarketState.sol and https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core#readme (CollateralTracker: 'its own market state including a global borrow index for compound interest calculations') at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api)
functionalObligations.note: `Ix` is added to the corpus element set, which carried only `Sh`. Index-based accrual and pro-rata shares coexist here and the corpus recorded one of them.

functionalObligations.text: An option seller borrows pooled liquidity and deploys it into a concentrated Uniswap V3 or V4 range; an option buyer borrows that same chunk back out of Uniswap and holds the underlying tokens, and it is the removal of the liquidity that creates the option.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ and https://panoptic.xyz/docs/product/streamia (accessed 2026-08-04); contracts/SemiFungiblePositionManagerV3.sol and contracts/SemiFungiblePositionManagerV4.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE inside the obligation. `Cl` names range positions and `Pl` names the shared credit pool, but nothing names lending an LP position as the underwriting primitive, nor the SFPM's ability to mint *negative* liquidity — burning Uniswap liquidity as a position is what manufactures a long option, and no element anticipates a composition of `Cl` and `Pl` in which the composition is the instrument.

functionalObligations.text: A position has no strike and no expiry: it is a tick range, up to four legs, encoded in one ERC-1155 tokenId, and it never expires and is never exercised at a price.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ (accessed 2026-08-04) — 'Panoptions are perpetual and never expire'; contracts/tokens/ERC1155Minimal.sol and contracts/types/LiquidityChunk.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, axis (a). `Op` names 'strike/expiry/collateralized settlement' and two of the three clauses are false. Stronger than the corpus recorded: it is not that the strike takes an unusual value, it is that the strike parameter has a different *type* — an interval of ticks rather than a price — so any formalism that quantifies over strikes cannot quantify over these.

functionalObligations.text: A buyer's position pays like a long option and a seller's like a short one — the removed liquidity's payoff is convex in the price of the underlying pair, which is why the protocol calls them options and why they are collateralised as such.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ and https://panoptic.xyz/docs/product/streamia (accessed 2026-08-04); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/panoptic-protocol/liquidations (Buying Power Requirement = notionalSize x (100% - S/K), accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: FLAGGED FORCED FIT, carried for the same reason the corpus carried it: the instrument is unambiguously an option economically and the vocabulary offers no alternative, while F4 and F5 falsify two of the symbol's three definitional clauses. RESIDUE inside the obligation: no element records that the payoff is *synthesised* from an AMM invariant — the LP payoff is a short-straddle-shaped function of `Cp` — rather than declared as a contract term.

functionalObligations.text: The payoff is realised continuously as the underlying range position's composition changes with price; closing a position burns it and returns tokens, and there is no terminal fixing to determine.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ and https://panoptic.xyz/docs/product/streamia (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, axis (b). Neither cash nor physical settlement as the axis means them — a third value the corpus's binary does not have, and the one case in this category where terminal settlement-price determination is not merely unnameable but inapplicable.

functionalObligations.text: The buyer pays no upfront premium and instead owes streamia, a per-block stream to the seller that accrues only while spot is inside the position's range.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://panoptic.xyz/docs/product/streamia (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: `Sr` names the accrual, axis (d) second value. It does not name that the stream IS the premium — that this accrual discharges the consideration for an option — which is why the corpus flagged it. Negative accumulated streamia is itself a liquidation trigger.

functionalObligations.text: The rate of streamia is the Uniswap swap fee the removed liquidity would have generated, multiplied by a spread multiplier that grows with how much of that specific chunk has been removed (VEGOID = 8, nu = 1/VEGOID).
functionalObligations.evidence: https://panoptic.xyz/docs/product/streamia (accessed 2026-08-04); VEGOID = 8 in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, axis (f), and a fourth value the corpus's axis does not enumerate. The premium is not modelled, quoted or matched — it is *generated* by realised trading activity in another protocol and then scaled by local utilisation. Beside model-priced, book-priced and quote-priced there is realised-AMM-fee-priced, and no element names any of the four.

functionalObligations.text: Sellers pay interest to PLPs on the liquidity they borrow, at a rate produced by a PID controller with a persistent rate-at-target bounded between 0.001 and 2.0 ether per 365 days and initialised at 0.04.
functionalObligations.evidence: MIN_RATE_AT_TARGET, MAX_RATE_AT_TARGET and INITIAL_RATE_AT_TARGET in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); https://panoptic.xyz/blog/panoptic-v2-is-coming (V1 deposit-fee model replaced by an interest-rate lending model, accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: `Pl` implies a rate exists. RESIDUE inside the obligation: nothing names a controller with memory — a rate that is a state variable moving between firings rather than a function of current utilisation. The corpus record predates this change entirely and does not mention interest at all.

functionalObligations.text: The counterparty to a buyer is whoever's liquidity chunk was removed, the funding for both sides comes from a shared pool, and the payoff shape is the AMM's own.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ and https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core#readme at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, axis (c), and the sharpest case of it: Panoptic is peer-to-peer in exposure, peer-to-pool in funding and AMM-derived in payoff — three of the corpus's axis-(c) values at once. An axis whose values are not mutually exclusive is not a partition, which is a fact about the proposed refinement of `Op` as much as about the current symbol.

functionalObligations.text: The RiskEngine computes a collateral requirement for a whole position set — spreads, strangles, iron condors and synthetics — and isAccountSolvent compares it to the account's balance, accounting for cross-collateralisation between token0 and token1 through CROSS_BUFFER_0 and CROSS_BUFFER_1.
functionalObligations.evidence: contracts/RiskEngine.sol (2,401 lines; isAccountSolvent, CROSS_BUFFER_0/1) at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 and https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core#readme (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/panoptic-protocol/liquidations (accessed 2026-08-04); RiskEngine.sol in scope at https://code4rena.com/audits/2025-12-panoptic-next-core (19 Dec 2025 - 7 Jan 2026, $56,000 USDC; accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: THE CORPUS DEMOTED `Ct` TO 'derived' AND THIS IS HALF OF WHY THE TABLES REJECT PANOPTIC. The threshold test is a standalone, separately audited 2,401-line contract whose entire purpose is this computation; it is as first-class as a mechanism gets. Promoted to the construction. The documented example — selling an OTM put starts at 20% collateralisation and rises as it moves in the money, Buying Power Requirement = notionalSize x (100% - S/K) — is the requirement `Ct` names.

functionalObligations.text: Collateral requirements scale with pool utilisation up to SATURATED_POOL_UTIL = 9,000,000, and leverage of up to 10x buying and 5x selling holds only under normal conditions and changes in response to pool utilisation.
functionalObligations.evidence: SATURATED_POOL_UTIL and BP_DECREASE_BUFFER in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. `Ct` tests a position against a requirement; nothing names a requirement that is a function of *pool* state, so a seller's margin can deteriorate because other accounts traded. This is a solvency coupling between users that the vocabulary represents as no coupling at all.

functionalObligations.text: The price source is the traded pool itself: an eight-slot sorted ring buffer giving a median tick, four exponential moving averages at 60, 120, 240 and 960 seconds combined as twapEMA = (6*fastEMA + 3*slowEMA + eonsEMA)/10, a clamp on how far a median observation may move, and MAX_TWAP_DELTA_DISPATCH = 513 ticks as the largest permitted gap between the current tick and the TWAP tick at dispatch.
functionalObligations.evidence: EMA_PERIODS = 60 + (120 << 24) + (240 << 48) + (960 << 72), MAX_CLAMP_DELTA, MAX_TWAP_DELTA_DISPATCH = 513 and the median ring buffer in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ ('Panoptic operates oracle-free by design', accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: THE OTHER HALF OF WHY THE TABLES REJECT PANOPTIC. The corpus carries no price-source element at all — no `Ex`, no `Tp` — so L1's first term is open, and 'oracle-free by design' means no *external* feed, not no price source. `Tp` is exactly right for an on-chain time-weighted price and is warranted here by `Cl`. Promoted to the construction; with `Tp` and `Ct` restored the rejection disappears and is shown to be a decomposition artefact. What `Tp` does not name: that the output is an *ensemble* of four values rather than one.

functionalObligations.text: Safe mode is the disjunction of an external-shock test (|currentTick - spotEMA| > MAX_TICKS_DELTA), an internal-disagreement test (|spotEMA - fastEMA| > MAX_TICKS_DELTA/2) and a divergence test (|medianTick - slowEMA| > MAX_TICKS_DELTA/2), OR-ed with a guardian-settable lockMode; when it is on, or when the Euclidean deviation of spot, latest and current from the median exceeds MAX_TICKS_DELTA, solvency is tested at all four ticks instead of one.
functionalObligations.evidence: isSafeMode, lockMode and getSolvencyTicks in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); contracts/PanopticGuardian.sol at the same commit; https://panoptic.xyz/docs/contracts/smart-contracts-overview (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE. `Gp` names the guardian's lock and nothing else. RESIDUE in two directions: nothing names an automatic, graduated tightening triggered by the price source distrusting its own internal state — this is a circuit breaker whose trigger is self-diagnosis, not an operator's judgement — and nothing names a solvency test that is a *conjunction over an ensemble whose cardinality is a function of the ensemble's own dispersion*. Neither `Ex` nor `Tp` can express a risk test at four prices at once. Numeric values of MAX_TICKS_DELTA, MAX_CLAMP_DELTA and TARGET_POOL_UTIL were not read and are UNKNOWN.

functionalObligations.text: A liquidator closes an insolvent account's positions and takes Bonus = min{Collateral Balance / 2, Collateral Requirement at TWAP - Collateral Balance at TWAP}.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://panoptic.xyz/docs/panoptic-protocol/liquidations (accessed 2026-08-04); getLiquidationBonus in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
functionalObligations.note: `Li` fits. Note that the bonus is computed at the TWAP tick rather than the current tick, so the liquidation incentive is denominated in the same ensemble F12 produces.

functionalObligations.text: A shortfall remaining after liquidation costs and bonus is absorbed first by a haircut on the account's unsettled premia.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core/blob/d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749/contracts/RiskEngine.sol — liquidation-bonus return docstring, 'the LeftRight-packed collateral remaining after liquidation costs and bonus; negative slots represent protocol loss before premia haircut' (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. `Sl` allocates loss to a claim class and `Tr` declares seniority over a loss event; between them they cannot express 'haircut the unpaid stream first'. The first absorber here is an accrued receivable — income already earned and not yet settled — subordinated ahead of the pool, which is a seniority claim over a flow rather than over a balance.

functionalObligations.text: What remains after the premia haircut is protocol loss borne by the CollateralTracker, that is by the PLPs pro rata.
functionalObligations.evidence: contracts/RiskEngine.sol ('negative slots represent protocol loss before premia haircut') at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents), against https://panoptic.xyz/docs/panoptic-protocol/liquidations (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: `Sl` fits and is added to the corpus element set, discharging L1's loss-absorption term alongside `Li` and L2's exit-liquidity clause. It also settles a documentation conflict: the docs say the pool will never incur a loss, the code returns protocol loss as a modelled outcome. The code is the evidence.

functionalObligations.text: A seller may force-exercise a buyer's out-of-range long position to reclaim the liquidity, paying the exercised user a fee that decays exponentially with distance from strike (FORCE_EXERCISE_COST = 30,000 scaled units, floored at ONE_BPS = 1000).
functionalObligations.evidence: exerciseCost, FORCE_EXERCISE_COST = 30_000 and ONE_BPS = 1000 in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Not liquidation — the target is solvent — and not exercise, since the holder does not elect it. Nothing names compulsion without distress: one user closing another's healthy position and compensating them for it.

functionalObligations.text: PanopticFactoryV3 and PanopticFactoryV4 will open an options market on any Uniswap V3 or V4 pool permissionlessly, on any ERC20 pair.
functionalObligations.evidence: contracts/PanopticFactoryV3.sol and contracts/PanopticFactoryV4.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Listing is factory deployment, so the instrument universe is unbounded and ungoverned — the opposite pole from the governed expiry calendars at Derive and Aevo and equally unnameable. The vocabulary has no symbol for a listing process at any point on that range.

functionalObligations.text: Every user action funnels through dispatch() / dispatchFrom(), which will revert when the current tick is further than MAX_TWAP_DELTA_DISPATCH from the TWAP tick.
functionalObligations.evidence: dispatch/dispatchFrom in https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core#readme and MAX_TWAP_DELTA_DISPATCH = 513 in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. A single entry point that admits or refuses every interaction on a price-agreement condition is neither a pause (`Gp`) nor a threshold test on a position (`Ct`) — it is an admission gate on the whole protocol, conditioned on the price source's internal consistency.

functionalObligations.text: Commissions on positions are split between the protocol, the PLPs and, where a builder code is present, the integrator whose interface constructed the call; long positions above a rehypothecation threshold receive credited shares.
functionalObligations.evidence: contracts/Builder.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 and https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core#readme (commissions, builder codes, rehypothecation threshold) (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api)
functionalObligations.note: `Fd` is candidate register and names the surplus split. It does not name attribution to whoever constructed the calldata, which is the novel part — a fee share that follows the interface rather than the capital or the flow.

functionalObligations.text: Administration is performed by Gnosis-Safe transactions against contracts that the factory deploys as fresh non-proxy instances, with a guardian able to override safe mode and lock or unlock pools.
functionalObligations.evidence: safe-txns-RiskEngine/ and gen_safetx.py at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749, contracts/PanopticGuardian.sol (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/contracts/smart-contracts-overview (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: `Up` is dropped from the corpus element set: stage 1 read no proxy, no initializer and no implementation slot in the V2 contracts, and the corpus asserts `Up` without an evidenced mechanism. Whether any component sits behind a proxy is UNKNOWN. `Tg` requires a delay and none is evidenced, so L15 does not arise because `Up` does not. RESIDUE: multisig administration of immutable, factory-deployed instances is a distinct control regime that neither `Up`, `Tg` nor `Gp` names.

functionalObligations.text: The protocol lends against, and prices with, the same Uniswap pool its instruments are written on, and mitigates the resulting manipulation channel with a median ring buffer, a four-EMA ensemble, a clamp on median movement, the dispatch TWAP-delta bound and safe mode.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core/blob/d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749/contracts/RiskEngine.sol (median buffer, EMA_PERIODS, MAX_CLAMP_DELTA, MAX_TWAP_DELTA_DISPATCH, isSafeMode) and https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core/tree/d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749/audits (2025-10-panoptic-v2.pdf, NM0701-FINAL_PANOPTIC_V2.pdf, code4rena-panoptic-next-core.md) (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE about the prohibition tables rather than the vocabulary. X2 ('Fl + manipulable Cp/Cl price + Pl/Cd') is NOT armed — there is no flash liquidity — yet the failure mode X2 guards against is this protocol's central design problem, and five named mechanisms exist for no other purpose than to mitigate it. A prohibition is armed or it is not; there is no way to record 'the failure mode is present and explicitly defended', so the table scores an unmitigated design and a purpose-built defence identically.

paper.title: Panoptic
paper.label: cat:opt:panoptic
paper.blurb: A venue that manufactures option-like payoffs out of concentrated liquidity positions rather than writing contracts, so its collateral, its pricing and its liquidation all run through an automated market maker. It is described as oracle-free, which is true of external feeds and false of prices.
paper.witnessReason: The second artefact. The corpus carried no price source for this venue at all, having read oracle-free as price-free, and demoted its collateral test --- a substantial audited risk engine --- to a derived consequence. The witness restores both: an on-chain time-weighted price is a price, and a risk engine is a threshold test. The rejection disappears with them.
paper.residueNote: That an option can be assembled from a liquidity range, rather than written as a contract, is the venue's whole design and has no expression here. The vocabulary has a symbol for the payoff and a symbol for the range, and no way to say that one is being built out of the other.
